title: symmetry + shrink Wc(q,t)->Wc(R,t) restore uses an inconsistent atom-pair set: hard crash `Missing ABF atom block` (or an old binary), then silently wrong high bands
symptom: Three layers. (a) Crash: `G0W0::build_spacetime failed at stage 'transform Wc(q,t) -> Wc(R,t), itau=0': ABACUS irreducible-sector W(q)->W(R) accumulation failed ... Missing ABF atom block while rotating the ABACUS q-space operator` (slurm FAILED 127:0) for MnTe (4 atoms, nspin=2, 15 pair classes in irreducible_sector.txt, including lower-triangle pairs (1,0),(2,0),(3,1)). (b) Silent wrongness: after patching the pair set, the symmetry+shrink SiC sg15 GW still gives `GW bandgap(eV): -126.7790101` with large positive/negative outliers in GW_band_spin_1.dat; the patch changed energies by 8.11 eV on average and up to 4668 eV per point but did not fix the physics. Related measured disagreement: for MnO2 sym+shrink, mpi1 vs mpi4 KS bands are identical and EXX differs by <=1e-5, yet GW_band_spin_1 high states differ by up to 129.7 eV and spin2 by up to 561.9 eV, while the band gap and spin1-k1-state1-eqp are identical. (c) A repeat of the already-fixed crash can just mean a stale binary: the MnTe job ran `/data/home/df_iopcas_ghj/app/librpa/LibRPA/build-cleancommit-20260427/chi0_main.exe` built at 2026-04-27 20:05:01, i.e. 46 seconds BEFORE the fix commit `b34d366` (20:05:47).
root_cause: (a) The direct W(q)->W(R) restore path in the symmetry lane collected full `(I,J)` atom pairs from `irreducible_sector.txt` (which contains lower-triangle pairs) instead of a consistent upper-triangle Hermitian pair set, so rotation tried to read blocks that were never generated - thrown at src/abacus_symmetry.cpp:2578 and wrapped into build_spacetime failure at src/epsilon.cpp:1362. (b) Under MPI>1, `restore_abacus_abf_full_qspace_operator()` sets `target_atom_pairs` to `collect_all_upper_atom_pairs(atom_nabf)` (src/epsilon.cpp:957), i.e. the restored `Wc_q_full` may hold only canonical-direction upper pairs, while `FT_Wc_q2R` / `CT_FT_Wc_q2R_freq2time` (src/epsilon.cpp:897-960 and 4823-4880) still allocates W(R) from the pre-restore `atpairs_unique`, fabricating non-existent lower-triangle zero blocks; `Wc_tau_R -> Wc_libri` is then a plain `=` assignment (src/gw.cpp:1348-1384), so those fabricated zeros overwrite the correct conjugate blocks derived from the upper triangle. The path only triggers when shrink is on, because the shrink branch unfolds Wc from the contracted basis, explicitly fills the Hermitian lower blocks and runs FT_Wc_q2R for every tau (src/gw.cpp:1288, 1322).
minimal_fix: Make the pair set consistent end to end instead of assuming both triangles: collect the atom-pair set directly from the restored `Wc_q_full` / `Wc_freq_q_full` in `FT_Wc_q2R` (src/epsilon.cpp:4492 and 4876) rather than from the pre-restore list, and never let a fabricated zero block overwrite a conjugated block in the `Wc_tau_R -> Wc_libri` assignment. The crash layer was fixed by commit `b34d366` (2026-04-27 20:05:47); before re-diagnosing any recurrence, resolve the executable the job actually used (`readlink -f`, `ls -l`, sha256) and compare it with the fix commit time/SHA, then rebuild and resubmit if the binary predates the fix. A stronger fix is still needed upstream in `restore_abacus_abf_full_qspace_operator()` / `symmetrize_abacus_abf_ibz_blocks()` / `rotate_abacus_abf_kspace_operator_blocks()`.
validation: For the crash: run MnO2-style shrink -> sym+shrink with the fixed binary and confirm both mpi1 and mpi4 walk through `Tranform Wc (q,t) -> (R,t)` and `Call libRI cal_Sigc` without the Missing-ABF-atom-block error (MnO2 completed on mpi1/mpi4, so nspin=2 and multi-MPI are not sufficient conditions). For provenance: `ls -l` timestamp and sha256 of chi0_main.exe versus `git log -1 --format=%ci <fix-commit>`, recorded in the run report next to the source commit. For the physics: dump `Wc_restored_fullq_*`, `Wc_input_qspace_*` and `Wc_unfold_tau0_*` and compare block by block against the symmetry-off reference, and compare the same physical quantity matrices between a paired symmetry-on and symmetry-off run of the SAME small regression case (both with shrink on) to find the first matrix where the two diverge.
avoid: Do not trust slurm COMPLETED, and do not stop at 'mpi1 == mpi4': in the MnO2 case the two MPI layouts agree while both are wrong relative to symmetry-off. Do not attribute a crash to a new root cause before proving which binary produced it - a stale `build-*/chi0_main.exe` in a shared app directory is the default trap in these lanes. Do not assume the q-index/layout header is the bug - both the ABACUS 29-IBZ products (`Cs_shrinked_data_0.txt`, `shrink_sinvS_0.txt`, `coulomb_cut_0.txt` first line 29, consistent with `Number of IBZ k-points (k stars): 29` in symrot_k.txt) and the shrink matrices themselves (their star covariance was verified to near machine precision) were checked and are correct. Note also that `use_shrink_chi = t` does nothing when `use_shrink_abfs = f`, because the contraction is decided by whether `sinvS` is non-empty (driver/read_data.cpp:713).
